headline: Majors hold above 200-day lines with momentum fading; positioning crowded and expensive; whale bid reverses after three weeks of selling onto exchanges.
paragraphs: All seven majors sit above their 200-day simple moving averages, and six of seven show completed golden crosses (XRP and DOGE lack them), which is the definition of an uptrend in the classical frame. Bitcoin is up 23.1% over the month and 0.2% over the week, down 0.9% on the day. Ethereum is up 31.1% monthly and 0.9% weekly, down 0.4% on the day. SOL and ADA tell a sharper story: both are up over 30% on the month but SOL is down 2.5% on the week (and 0.7% on the day) while ADA is up 9.1% weekly (down 0.0% daily). The regime is higher lows and higher highs in the 30-day frame, but intraweek chop and single-day weakness across most symbols suggest the momentum pulse is easing. This is not a trend reversal; it is a rest inside a trend.

Momentum diverges from structure in ways that matter. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 59.9 and MACD remains below its signal line, which means price made a fresh 30-day push higher without MACD confirming it. Ethereum shows the same pattern: RSI-14 at 62.2, MACD below signal. SOL, XRP, and BTC are all in the 59-61 RSI range, neutral territory where they have room to accelerate but also room to roll. BNB is the outlier: RSI-14 at 68.5 with MACD above signal, a live positive divergence between momentum and price after a 32.2% monthly gain and 8.0% weekly surge. DOGE and ADA also have MACD above signal despite RSI in the 59-61 band, which reads as early upside momentum forming rather than exhaustion. The tape shows no uniform exhaustion signal, but it does show several assets (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP) where momentum has not kept pace with price, a classic lag before either a continuation shove or a near-term pullback.

Derivatives positioning is crowded, expensive, and tilted long across the board. Bitcoin perpetual funding is 0.48% per 8 hours (5.2% annualized), above zero, which means longs are paying shorts to hold; open interest is 2.17 billion dollars. Ethereum funding is 0.93% per 8 hours (10.2% annualized) on 1.51 billion in open interest, nearly double Bitcoin's rate. SOL is the sole exception: negative 0.87% per 8 hours (negative 9.5% annualized) on 288 million in open interest, meaning shorts are paying longs, a signal that the long side has found a ceiling. XRP and DOGE both show positive 1.0% per 8 hours (11.0% annualized), the highest on the sheet. Long-to-short ratios are extreme: DOGE at 3.26 to 1, XRP at 2.31 to 1, and SOL at 1.9 to 1. Bitcoin and Ethereum are more moderate at 1.26 and 1.24, but still biased long. Liquidations in the last 6 to 11 hours show more long-side pain than short-side: in Bitcoin, 1.81 million in long liquidations versus 240 thousand in shorts; in Ethereum, 2.9 million in long liquidations versus 94 thousand in shorts. This is the tape of a market where leverage has accumulated on the bullish side and the short end is lightly positioned, a structure that can accelerate further if stops do not trigger, but one that is vulnerable if the flow tide turns.

Stablecoin float stands at 310.2 billion dollars, up 1.36% over the past month, a modest build in dry powder that does not scream urgency either way. Bitcoin ETF flows show 174.6 million inflow on the latest session (04 Sep) with 986.7 million net inflow over the last five sessions and three same-direction days, a consistent traditional-finance bid. Ethereum ETF inflow was 25.9 million on the latest session with 215.3 million over five sessions, but only two same-direction days, indicating less conviction. Whale activity over the past week (ending 09 Sep) shows 28.1 million moving off exchanges, a reversal after three consecutive weeks of net inflow (Aug 19 through Sep 02 saw 333 million, 1.2 billion, and 49 million move onto exchanges respectively). Bitcoin whales have been ambiguous: 134.1 million net out over the week, but this masks 1.63 billion outflow from Coinbase (cold storage signal) offset by 1.50 billion inflow elsewhere. Ethereum whales moved 106.1 million onto exchanges over the week, inverse to Bitcoin, suggesting divergent risk positioning between the two.

Sentiment sits at 66 on the Fear and Greed Index, labeled Greed, within a 30-day range of 27 to 74. The crowd is confident but not euphoric; the tape does not confirm that confidence. Bitcoin is 37.2% below its 12-month high, Ethereum 47.4%, and SOL 58.4%. These are not fresh all-time highs; they are recoveries from deeper lows. The day's largest movers are scattered: VVV and FF each up over 20%, DOT up 14.25%, while MORPHO, PENDLE, and TIA are down between 4.9% and 6.1%. Sideways action at the altcoin level amid major-cap strength suggests rotation rather than broad conviction. Network fees on Bitcoin are mild at 4 satoshis per byte fastest (3 for the hour rate), and difficulty is up 1.3% with 1555 blocks until the next retarget, unremarkable data points.

Watch for a MACD cross above signal on Bitcoin or Ethereum, which would align momentum with the recent price higher and confirm the uptrend continuation. Watch for SOL funding to flip positive, which would signal the short squeeze is complete and the long overhang has eased. Watch the weekly whale flow direction: if the current week ending Sep 09 reversal (off exchanges) continues into next week, cold storage accumulation may be reasserting, a supply-side floor. Watch whether long-side liquidations accelerate on any 2-3% move lower, which would test whether the crowded positioning fractures or holds. None of these are forecasts; they are conditions in the data that would tell a reader the picture changed.
